_about: Water (1) + acetic acid (2) + ethyl acetate (3): liquid-liquid tie lines at 303.15 and 313.15 K and 101.0 kPa, from Toikka et al. (2014). Phase I is the water-rich liquid, phase II the ester-rich liquid. Rows: T in K, the mole fractions of water, acetic acid and ethyl acetate in phase I, the same in phase II, and the combined expanded uncertainty the record states for the measured mole fractions of phase I and of phase II (null where the record gives none).

source.citation: M. Toikka, A. A. Samarov, M. Trofimova, A. Golikova, N. Tsvetov, Solubility, liquid-liquid equilibrium and critical states for the quaternary system acetic acid-ethanol-ethyl acetate-water at 303.15 K and 313.15 K, Fluid Phase Equilib. 373 (2014) 72-79
source.access: Journal article is subscription-only; the same data is public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive (NIST open license).
source.tables: ThermoML record, PureOrMixtureData 4 (acetic acid + ethyl acetate + water, phases liquid mixture 1 and 2, 14 rows): v1 T; v2 mole fraction of acetic acid in liquid 1; p1 ethyl acetate in liquid 1; p2 acetic acid in liquid 2; p3 ethyl acetate in liquid 2. The table number in the article was not checked (article not open).

notes: The mole fraction of water in each liquid is 1 minus the other two (not stored in the record), rounded to the record's 3 decimals. u_I is the record's uncertainty of ethyl acetate in liquid 1, u_II that of acetic acid in liquid 2 (the record gives none for the other measured values). The two rows without acetic acid are the binary water + ethyl acetate edge: their ester-rich liquid holds 0.142 (303.15 K) and 0.162 (313.15 K) water, where the binary sets fitted in CHEPTA (Grande and Marschoff 2005) give 0.1885 and 0.2111.
